author: NorthEast News Desk
body: U.S. stocks moved lower Thursday as rising Treasury yields, higher oil prices and August producer-price data increased concern that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates next week.

Reuters reported that the S&P 500, Nasdaq and Dow were each down around six-tenths of a percent during the session. Nvidia and Micron fell, while Apple advanced a day after introducing its folding phone. The figures describe intraday trading and are not live prices.

The 10-year Treasury yield reached its highest level in nearly three years, while the 30-year yield touched a more than 19-year high. Brent crude’s jump to about $107 a barrel added to inflation pressure as disruptions affected major energy routes.

Producer prices rose in line with expectations on a monthly basis, with energy costs rebounding. Futures markets increased the implied chance of a quarter-point Fed increase at the coming meeting. Investors now turn to Friday’s consumer-price report for a broader read on inflation. Higher yields can pressure stock valuations by raising borrowing costs and improving returns available from bonds.
dek: Major U.S. indexes declined Thursday as higher energy costs and producer-price data strengthened expectations for tighter Federal Reserve policy.
headline: Wall Street falls as Treasury yields and inflation fears rise
